clue.text: Old minstrel beginning to junket on fresh gruel

indicators.note: the beginning of the word junket is its opening letter, which is all that is taken

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fresh signals that the letters of gruel are made new, set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A medieval entertainer starts on a sweet dessert served over newly made porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' looks like it describes the gruel, but it signals the rearrangement of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A jongleur was an itinerant medieval entertainer who sang and recited, so the word names an old minstrel.

clue.text: Basically you look quite humorous strumming these

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of each word is its final letter, so the bottoms of the four words are taken

explanation.surface: Anyone playing small guitars looks rather comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basically' picks the base, that is the last letter, of each of you, look, quite and humorous.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukes is short for ukuleles, small four-stringed instruments that are strummed.

clue.text: Initially set contract iPhone to divert

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word set
to contract a word is to shorten it, here by cutting its final letter

parts.note: the brand name of the Apple phone, taken as its letters

explanation.surface: Advice to arrange a mobile phone deal and then redirect it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a phone deal but means shorten: IPHONE loses its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To siphon funds or water is to draw them off and divert them elsewhere.

clue.text: Fly attracted to huge English bush

parts.note: to fly is to rush along, which is to tear
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: An insect is drawn to a big English shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads as an insect but is the verb meaning to hurry, TEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a kind of rose shrub with a scent said to recall tea, so it is a bush.

clue.text: Make changes — vote in an alternative!

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters is asked for, so the preceding words are reordered

explanation.surface: A political slogan urging reform by voting for a different candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges the letters of VOTE IN AN; the exclamation reads as a campaign slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to introduce new methods, that is to make changes.

clue.text: Devotees of old Chinese whisper mix-ups

indicators.note: a whisper is something spoken, so the word for mix-ups is heard rather than written

parts.note: mix-ups are muddles or confusions

explanation.surface: The game Chinese whispers famously produces garbled messages.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the party game Chinese whispers; the old Chinese is the sage Confucius.
explanation.definitionFit: Confucians follow the teaching of Confucius, the ancient Chinese philosopher.

clue.text: Extremely ethical environmentalist cleaned out small hole

indicators.note: each of the three words is emptied of its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A highly principled green campaigner tidied up a little opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like the indicator but is itself fodder: 'cleaned out' empties all three words, giving EY, EL and ET.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small round hole, often reinforced, for a lace or cord to pass through.

clue.text: Where you might unship old copper compound, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver the phrase is to be spoken aloud

parts.note: D stood for the old British penny, a copper coin, and an oxide is a chemical compound

explanation.surface: A chemistry question about an old copper compound and where cargo is unloaded.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the pre-decimal penny, plus OXIDE said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is unloaded at the side of a dock, so that is where you might unship goods.

clue.text: Like a secluded corner for it?

definitions.meaning: a playful adjective meaning resembling a nook or snug corner
it is a coy word for sex, as is this slang term

explanation.surface: A question whether a quiet corner is suitable for a sexual encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for sexual activity, also read jokingly as an adjective formed from nook.

clue.text: Anglers regularly disappearing for long periods

indicators.note: every other letter of the word anglers drops out at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Fishermen keep vanishing for lengthy spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly disappearing' removes the second, fourth and sixth letters of Anglers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages, in the informal sense, are very long stretches of time.

clue.text: Ring Carrie or Christine?

parts.note: reads like a choice of whom to telephone, but each is the title of a frightening movie

explanation.surface: Wondering whether to phone one woman or another.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring (from Japan), Carrie and Christine (both from Stephen King novels) are all scary films.
explanation.definitionFit: Each title names an example of a scary genre of cinema, so the clue asks what they are.

clue.text: Old cardinal who's not a sexist

definitions.meaning: John Henry ... was a nineteenth-century English cardinal
a modern man who rejects sexism and shares domestic work

explanation.surface: A remark that a former cardinal was no chauvinist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal John Henry Newman is the historic churchman; a new man is a caring, non-sexist modern male.

clue.text: Record describes capricious regent in Balkan state

indicators.note: to describe is to draw round, as in describing a circle, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a mono is a recording in monophonic sound

indicators.note: capricious means unpredictable, so the letters of regent are jumbled

explanation.surface: A document detailing a wayward ruler of a south-east European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' is used in its geometric sense, to draw a line round, so the record encloses the reordered ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Montenegro is a small country in the Balkans on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Thus carrying pet back and forth to be clipped

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: and forth says the same word follows read the normal way
back tells the solver to read the word for pet in reverse

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
the same pet read the second time forwards

explanation.surface: Carting an animal to and fro to have it trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped' is a musical term here, not a haircut; 'back' and 'and forth' read the same pet in both directions inside the word for thus.
explanation.definitionFit: In music staccato notes are short and detached, so the playing is clipped.

clue.text: Irish individual hoarding gold, a tradable commodity

indicators.note: hoarding means keeping stored away inside, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: an individual is one
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An Irish person stockpiling gold as a marketable asset.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron ore is a raw material mined and traded worldwide, so it is a commodity.

clue.text: Dawn is ushered in by ruddy bird

indicators.note: being ushered in by something means coming after it, so the word for dawn follows

parts.note: ruddy means red
the dawn of something is its start

explanation.surface: Daybreak heralded by a reddish songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like daybreak but means a beginning, START.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a rusty-red tail.

clue.text: Anaesthetist's comparatively sober

definitions.meaning: an anaesthetist is someone who puts patients under, one who sedates
more calm and composed than another

explanation.surface: A remark that a doctor is relatively serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as agent noun it is one who sedates; read as comparative it is more staid.

clue.text: Former African dictator, extremely electable candidate

parts.note: ex means former
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: the extremes of the word electable are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A one-time African tyrant presented as a very electable nominee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the end letters of electable, E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting an exam is a candidate in that test.

clue.text: Float and line cast over inlet? On the contrary

indicators.note: cast over describes one piece placed above another in a down entry
on the contrary reverses the stated order, so the inlet goes above the line

parts.note: an arm of the sea is an inlet
a band is a stripe or line

explanation.surface: Fishing gear: a float and a line cast over a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says line over inlet; 'On the contrary' swaps that, putting ARM above BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable band worn on the upper arm keeps a child afloat in water.

clue.text: Kindle design accepted by Green movement

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so one piece sits inside the other
movement shifts the letters of Green about

parts.note: an end is a design, aim or purpose

explanation.surface: An e-reader layout taken up by an environmental campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' looks like the e-reader but means arouse. 'movement' turns GREEN into ENGER, which takes in END.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle feelings is to arouse them, to bring them into being.

clue.text: Baffled bachelor becoming new groom

indicators.note: becoming signals one letter turning into another

parts.note: baffled means beaten, defeated by a problem

explanation.surface: A confused single man transforms into a bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like a bridegroom but is the verb to tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom something is to tidy it, to make it neat.

clue.text: He loves to tell Spooner's fish joke

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a bass is a fish
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A man who enjoys telling a fishy joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts of BASS GAG gives GAS BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is a person who talks too much, someone who loves to tell.

clue.text: Somewhat slowly undergoing contraction by third quarter

indicators.note: the musical term is shortened by a third of its length, losing its first three letters

parts.note: larghetto is the musical direction meaning fairly slowly

explanation.surface: A sluggish muscle contraction in the third quarter of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: LARGHETTO has nine letters; cutting a third, LAR, leaves the city district.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a quarter of a city where a minority group is concentrated.

clue.text: Wretched Liberal willing to embrace leader of Tories

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: amenable means willing

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A miserable Liberal ready to hug the Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts T inside AMENABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentable means deplorable or pitiful, so wretched.

clue.text: Song in which black sheep gets shorn

indicators.note: shearing takes off the outside, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a black sheep is an outcast, a pariah

explanation.surface: A ditty about a black sheep having its fleece clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black sheep' is the outcast PARIAH; 'gets shorn' trims off P and H.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera.

clue.text: Behead clergyman shortly

indicators.note: to behead a word is to remove its first letter

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman of a cathedral

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to decapitate a priest soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behead' removes the C from CANON.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon, in a short while.

clue.text: Fluff found in belly of lesser rorqual

indicators.note: the belly of the phrase is its inside, where the letters sit across the two words

explanation.surface: Lint discovered in the stomach of a small whale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluff' looks like lint but means a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluff is a blunder or mistake, as when an actor fluffs a line.

clue.text: "Noun" in Roget represented as N

parts.note: N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun

indicators.note: represented means presented again, so the letters of in Roget are set out anew

explanation.surface: A note on how a thesaurus marks a noun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges IN ROGET to ITROGEN, after N. N is the chemical symbol for the element.
explanation.definitionFit: N is the chemical symbol for this gaseous element.
